capitals.name: Belize City
capitals.note: Infobox "Belize City (1862-1971); Belmopan (1971-1981)"; the page gives no capital for the settlement before 1862, Belize City is the researcher's reading.

correction.text: 'the area between the Hondo and the Belize rivers' where the Baymen could log (Treaty of Versailles, 1783)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no row before Belize (1983). The pages give rivers, not places: Corozal, Orange Walk and a 30 km ring round Belize City are the researcher's reading of 'between the Hondo and Belize rivers'. No area on either page.

correction.text: 'the Convention of London (1786) expanded this concession to include the area between the Belize and Sibun rivers'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Belize district is the researcher's reading of the land between the Belize and Sibun rivers. The settlement stayed a 'British settlement' until 1862; Spain 'never attempted to reclaim the area after 1798'.

correction.text: the colony to the Sarstoon after the Wyke-Aycinena Treaty of 1859: 'Guatemala agreed to recognize Britain's sovereignty over the area'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Modern Belize is the shape (the gazetteer resolves it to 84 cells, about 21,200 km2); the BH page gives no area. The Guatemalan claim (12,272 km2 or 'roughly 53% of Belizean territory') is a claim of 1999, not a change of the shape.

region.text: the logging settlement 'between the Hondo and Belize rivers'

ledger.note: 25 November 1783: the Treaty of Versailles recognises the British settlement in the Bay of Honduras. 'The 1783 Treaty of Versailles marked where the Baymen could log between the Hondo and Belize rivers'; infobox 'Treaty of Versailles: 25 November 1783' and 'British settlement (1783-1862)'.

region.text: the land between the Belize and Sibun rivers

ledger.note: 1786: the Convention of London extends the settlement to the Sibun. 'The 1786 Anglo-Spanish Convention was signed to extend the logging border down to the Sibun river.' The page gives only the year; the Belize district is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the south and the interior to the Sarstoon: 'Beginning at the mouth of the River Sarstoon in the Bay of Honduras'

ledger.note: 1859: the Wyke-Aycinena Treaty fixes the southern boundary at the Sarstoon. 'In the Wyke–Aycinena Treaty of 1859, Guatemala agreed to recognize Britain's sovereignty over the area.' The page gives the year and the Sarstoon; the three districts are the researcher's reading.

12 May 1862: the Settlement of Belize becomes the colony of British Honduras. 'In 1862 the Settlement of Belize in the Bay of Honduras was declared a British colony called British Honduras'; infobox 12 May 1862.
1971: the capital moves from Belize City to Belmopan. Infobox: 'Belize City (1862-1971); Belmopan (1971-1981).'
1 June 1973: British Honduras is renamed Belize. 'On 1 June 1973, the colony's name was changed to Belize in anticipation of independence.'
21 September 1981: Belize becomes independent. 'independence came to Belize on 21 September 1981, without an agreement with Guatemala'; self-government had come on 1 January 1964.

wars.name: Belizean–Guatemalan territorial dispute
wars.outcome: A diplomatic dispute with no fighting: Guatemala recognised British sovereignty in 1859 but later claimed the south; its 1999 claim 'amounts to 12,272 km2 ... or roughly 53% of Belizean territory'.
wars.note: No territorial result before 1981 and no dated campaign, so no contest zone is drawn.

certainty.note: The settlement's limits are rivers (Hondo, Belize, Sibun), not surveyed lines; the Spanish crown never ceded sovereignty on the pages opened.
The Sarstoon boundary of the 1859 treaty is a treaty line, but Guatemala disputed it throughout; the western frontier is not described on the pages opened.

notes:
Cliopatria has no British Honduras row (its Belize row starts in 1983; the British Colonial Empire row 1706-1999 is an aggregate). The two pages give the settlement's limits as rivers; the district-level regions are the researcher's reading. The pre-1862 capital is not given on the pages.
The Mexican frontier (the Hondo river, with the 1893 treaty) is not dated on either page; a gap-filler should open the 'Belize' history page. The Mosquito Coast and the Bay Islands are not part of this state.
Type colony: drawn as a vassal tint of the metropole (rule 4); counterpart spanish-empire has no Belize shape of its own.
